introduction: The `afspec` budget-cap rendering layer adds a `max_tokens` optional parameter to the Python and Go rendering functions, applying a two-level progressive truncation strategy (drop architecture, then slim test-spec assertions) so that downstream consumers such as `assemble_context()` can cap rendered spec content at a token target without manual truncation.

correctness_properties.title: No-budget render is byte-identical to legacy render
correctness_properties.invariant: `render_individual(spec, max_tokens=None)` returns a dict byte-identical to the pre-budget-cap `render_individual(spec)`, and `RenderIndividual()` (no options) returns a map identical to the pre-budget-cap `RenderIndividual()`

correctness_properties.title: Budget-capped render token sum is within budget when achievable
correctness_properties.for_any: any `Spec` value and any positive integer M
correctness_properties.invariant: if `render_individual(spec, max_tokens=M)` returns a dict D, then either `sum(estimate_tokens(v) for v in D.values()) <= M` or D is the Level 2 render (no further truncation is possible)

correctness_properties.title: Level 1 removes architecture key when present
correctness_properties.for_any: any `Spec` value that has an `architecture` section
correctness_properties.invariant: when Level 1 truncation is applied, the result dict does not contain the `architecture` key

correctness_properties.title: Level 2 slim render omits verbose assertion fields
correctness_properties.for_any: any `TestSpec` value with at least one test case entry
correctness_properties.invariant: `_render_test_spec_slim(ts)` produces a string that does not contain `assertion_pseudocode`, `input`, or `expected` content from any test case entry

correctness_properties.title: Python and Go produce structurally equivalent output for any spec and budget
correctness_properties.for_any: any `Spec` value and any positive integer N
correctness_properties.invariant: `render_individual(spec, max_tokens=N)` and `RenderIndividual(WithMaxTokens(N))` produce dicts with the same set of keys present and the same truncation level applied

correctness_properties.title: PRD body is never absent from any render
correctness_properties.invariant: the PRD body content is present in the output of `render_individual`, `render_individual_scoped`, and `render_combined` at every truncation level

correctness_properties.title: Zero or negative max_tokens is equivalent to no budget
correctness_properties.invariant: `render_individual(spec, max_tokens=0)` returns a dict identical to `render_individual(spec, max_tokens=None)`, and similarly for `render_individual_scoped` and `render_combined`

execution_paths.title: Python render_individual with budget cap — Level 1 truncation applied

steps.action: calls `render_individual(spec, max_tokens=M)` where the spec has an `architecture` section and the Level 0 render exceeds M tokens
renders all artifacts at Level 0 and sums `estimate_tokens(v)` for all values in the result dict
detects that the sum exceeds M; applies Level 1 by removing the `architecture` key from the result dict
re-sums token estimates; detects that the sum is now ≤ M
returns the Level 1 dict[str, str] to the caller
receives dict[str, str] without the `architecture` key, with estimated token sum ≤ M

execution_paths.title: Python render_individual with budget cap — Level 2 truncation applied

steps.action: calls `render_individual(spec, max_tokens=M)` where the spec has an `architecture` section but even Level 1 exceeds M tokens
renders at Level 0, sums token estimates, detects budget exceeded
applies Level 1 (drops `architecture` key), re-sums, detects budget still exceeded
applies Level 2: calls `_render_test_spec_slim` to re-render the test spec without verbose assertion fields
returns the Level 2 dict[str, str] to the caller regardless of whether it fits within M
receives dict[str, str] without `architecture` key and with slimmed test spec entries

execution_paths.title: Go RenderIndividual with WithMaxTokens — end-to-end budget cap flow

steps.action: calls `spec.RenderIndividual(WithMaxTokens(N))` on a `*Spec` value
parses the `RenderOption` via `WithMaxTokens`, sets the token budget on the unexported `renderConfig`
renders all artifacts at Level 0 and sums `EstimateTokens(v)` for all values in the result map
applies the same two-level progressive truncation evaluation loop as the Python implementation
returns `map[string]string` to the caller at the appropriate truncation level
receives `map[string]string` with the same structural properties as the Python equivalent call

execution_paths.title: assemble_context end-to-end — budget-capped spec rendering in agent session

steps.action: determines the token budget M for spec content in the system prompt
calls `render_individual(spec, max_tokens=M)` (Python) for each spec in scope
applies the progressive truncation evaluation loop (Level 0 → Level 1 → Level 2) using `estimate_tokens` to evaluate each level
re-renders the `TestSpec` without verbose assertion fields if Level 2 is reached
returns dict[str, str] at the appropriate truncation level to `assemble_context()`
concatenates the returned artifact strings into the system prompt, which now fits within the token budget

error_handling.condition: the `Spec` has no `TestSpec` when Level 2 slim rendering is applied
error_handling.behavior: the test spec section is rendered as absent or empty; no error is raised

error_handling.condition: `WithMaxTokens(0)` or a negative value is passed to a Go rendering method
